conviction_note: Two primary-document facts pull opposite ways and roughly cancel: a run of beats against its own guide (Q1 at the top end, Q2 above the top end) argues for a Q3 revenue beat, while the company's own 'H2 about 15% above H1' framework (about $119.4M) is already fully absorbed by consensus Q3 $57.5M plus Q4 $62.4M, so a Q3 beat without an H2 raise implies a Q4 guide at or below the Street, and the last two Q4/Q1 guides drew about -5% pre-market. Beats on this name have bought about +1%. Sum of findings -0.2, p_up 50, abs_move 6 with no usable option chain, so the scaled number is 0.

findings.finding: The company has beaten its own revenue guide two quarters running. Q1 2026 came in at $48.5M, the top of its $45-49M guide. Q2 2026 came in at $55.3M, above the top of its $51-55M guide and +4.8% over a roughly $52.8M consensus. On the Q2 call management said unit sales were running above plan and that it had 'some orders already in hand into Q3 and even in Q4'. That pattern points to Q3 near the $60M top of the guide, against a $57.5-58.6M consensus (about +3.5% at $59.5M).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 2026 beat above the top of the guide moved the stock about +1% to +1.5% ('barely budged', AAII and webull summaries). The Q1 2026 top-end beat drew about +1.5% per a low-quality auto-generated source. The Q3 2025 beat drew about -5% pre-market because the Q4 guide disappointed (https://www.itiger.com/news/1142228974). Beats alone have bought little.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus at $57.5M sits on the guide midpoint, not near the top where the last two quarters landed. If the Street had extrapolated the beat pattern, Q3 estimates would sit at $59-60M; only Chartmill's $58.6M leans that way.
findings.independence: The Q1 result against its guide comes from a separate release: https://www.streetinsider.com/Press+Releases/Kornit+Digital+Reports+First+Quarter+2026+Results/26481386.html. Shares the Q2 call with finding 2.

findings.finding: On the Q2 call the CFO framed H2 2026 revenue as about 15% above H1, which is about $119.4M on H1 of $103.8M. Consensus Q3 $57.5M plus Q4 $62.4M = $119.9M already sits on that framework. So if Q3 beats (about $59.5-60M) and management only reiterates H2, the implied Q4 is about $59.5-60M, below the $62.4M Street Q4. The guide, not the beat, is the line at risk unless the H2 framework is raised.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q3 2025 print (Nov 2025) beat but guided Q4 $56-60M and drew -5.03% pre-market (https://www.itiger.com/news/1142228974). The Q4 2025 print (Feb 2026) guided Q1 cautiously and drew about -5.5% pre-market (https://www.chartmill.com/news/KRNT/Chartmill-41715-KORNIT-DIGITAL-LTD-NASDAQKRNT-Reports-Mixed-Q4-2025-Results-Shares-Drop-on-Revenue-Miss). At Q2 2026 the guide was raised (Q3 $55-60M, FY to high single-digit growth) and the stock still moved only about +1%. This name has traded on the guide.
findings.why_not_priced: Previews quote the Q3 guide and consensus separately and do not show that the Q4 consensus already uses the whole H2 envelope. If that were priced, the Q4 consensus would sit nearer $60M, or the stock would not have held near $18 into November. It has fallen about 5% in five days, which may be partly this.
findings.independence: Same document as finding 1. The FY framing ('high single-digit growth' on FY2025 revenue of $208.2M, about $225M) gives the same envelope: https://www.chartmill.com/news/KRNT/Chartmill-41715-KORNIT-DIGITAL-LTD-NASDAQKRNT-Reports-Mixed-Q4-2025-Results-Shares-Drop-on-Revenue-Miss for FY2025. Q4 consensus $62.4M is from the Benzinga snippet only.

findings.finding: The subscription (AIC) metrics are compounding fast. ARR was $26.8M at Q1 2026 and $33.8M at Q2 2026 (+79% YoY), AIC revenue grew +112% YoY in Q2, and total contract value is about $142M. Management called AIC 'a major growth engine in H2 versus H1'. Another sequential step-up in ARR (to about $40M) would support the quality of the beat.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: ARR +79% at Q2 bought about +1% in total. The AIC shift has been the bull narrative since 2025, and the Morgan Stanley Nov-2025 downgrade argued the capex-to-opex shift would dampen growth.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The ARR trajectory is public, and only a step-up above trend (about $40M or more) would be new. Small for that reason.
findings.independence: The Q1 ARR figure is from a different release: https://thedeadpixelssociety.com/kornit-digital-reports-stronger-momentum-as-recurring-revenue-strategy-accelerates/

findings.finding: Amazon Merch on Demand, historically a large Kornit print-on-demand channel, moved on 2026-06-01 to tiered royalties that halve the default royalty for creators with under 15% external traffic ($4.88 to $2.44 on a $19.99 tee, per a vendor blog). That could thin design supply and volume on a channel printed on Kornit systems during Q3. On the Q2 call (2026-08-12) management did not name Amazon, declined to characterise its 'global strategic customer', and said most strategic customers were growing.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No release isolates this customer. The stock historically moved hard on Amazon-related volume commentary, but no dated source in this hunt shows that.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a creator-side policy change reported only in seller blogs, with no unit data. If it were priced, there would be analyst questions on it or a note; none was found.
findings.independence: Proxy, and the source is a tool vendor with commercial interest. Second secondary source: https://amzprep.com/amazon-merch-on-demand/. The company's own Q2 call says strategic customers are growing (https://www.webull.com/news/15429991240320000), which argues against it, so it is sized small.

findings.finding: Etsy, a marketplace dense in personalised and print-on-demand goods, reported Q3 2026 (July-Sept) GMS +8.8% YoY to $2.65B, an acceleration, and guided Q4 GMS +5-7%. That is a broad read that custom-product consumer demand held up in Kornit's Q3 and into peak season.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None for this line. Kornit has never been shown to trade on Etsy prints.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a peer-channel print after Kornit last spoke. It is unlinked: the article does not mention apparel or print-on-demand, so it is a weak proxy, mostly priced into general sentiment.
findings.independence: Proxy. A second report of the same print: https://grafa.com/en/news/united-states/etsy-q3-2026-revenue-rises-10-9-percent

findings.finding: The shekel held near NIS 2.95/$ through Q3 2026 (BoI representative rate 2026-08-17; a further 0.6% appreciation to 2026-09-01), about 12% stronger than a year earlier. In Q1 2026 Kornit attributed about 190bp of gross-margin decline to the shekel plus tariffs. That pressures the 0-3% adj. EBITDA guide, although the guide was set on 2026-08-12 with the rate already known.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q1 2026 margin hit from FX and tariffs coincided with a small positive reaction. FX has not driven a move on its own.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced. The rate was known when the guide was set, so it sits inside the guide and is sized near 0.
findings.independence: Globes on the August rate: https://en.globes.co.il/en/article-1001551946. Q1 attribution summary: https://finance.yahoo.com/news/kornit-digital-q1-earnings-call-160723593.html

findings.finding: Q2 2026 gross margin (47.4% non-GAAP) included a net tariff benefit of about $830k from a $2M tariff refund, worth about 150bp on $55.3M. Without a repeat, Q3 gross margin has a tougher sequential comparison, though management expects consumables mix to expand margin in H2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 print with the refund-inflated margin moved about +1%. The refund did not visibly move the stock.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a one-off in the prior quarter that analysts can strip out. Mostly priced, and sized as a fraction.
findings.independence: The call transcript states the same figure: https://www.webull.com/news/15429991240320000 (same company, one fact).

findings.finding: Capital return and balance sheet: $37.5M was repurchased in H1 2026, about $60M remains on the $100M authorization, and cash, deposits and securities were about $451M at 2026-06-30, roughly 63% of the about $713M market cap at $16.60. Continued buybacks reported for Q3, or an expanded program, would cushion a guide disappointment.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The new $100M program (Nov 2025, with the CFO transition) coincided with the -5% Q3 2025 reaction, so it did not offset a weak guide then.
findings.why_not_priced: It is known. It only matters as a floor and as possible news of an expanded authorization. Small.
